topic: Hip fracture analgesia and nerve block
usual_baseline: Nerve block use is low and poorly documented: fascia iliaca block in 2.0% [1715], 24.5% [1612], 35% [1381] and 65% [1732]; documented within 2 h in 6.4% [1769]. Contraindications were documented in 0% without a block [1732]. Regular postoperative paracetamol 3 g/day was given to 16% [1679].
fix_that_works: Teaching plus an enforced proforma with FICB sign-off raised block rate from 24.5% to 44.3% [1612]. Three PDSA cycles lifted block rate from 2.0% to 22.6% [1715]. Nurse-led audit and feedback raised postoperative paracetamol from 16% to 60% [1679]. An analgesia checklist cut time to first analgesia from 130 to 38.8 min and to FICB from 228 to 63.4 min [1732].
fix_that_fails: Practical sessions and a checklist did not raise FICB uptake (65% to 65%, p=0.74) or pain re-evaluation within 30 min (52.5% to 50%) [1732]. Preoperative paracetamol did not improve (9% to 16%, p=0.13) [1679]. The 50% block target was not met [1715].
consultant_advice: FICB rates are commonly audited. The better questions are time to block, documented reason when not given, and pain reassessment. Timing is often missing (43.2% of episodes with no block timing [1769]), so fix recording first with a mandatory timestamp.
